name: The Bodie Convergence
summary: Months after the archivist, the PCs quietly rationalize the strangeness away — until one of them (the Control-seeker archetype, off-screen) sends the others individual pretexts to converge on Bodie SHP, a Gold Country ghost town six hours away. A storm traps them; a 141-year-old mining-crew ledger has four of their names on it (a fifth entry water-damaged illegible); a wartime federal annex on the site has a plaque nobody wants to talk about; one of them accidentally casts in front of the others and it lands. The record-vs-memory phenomenon they investigated with Bea now happens to them.
hooks: The DM's absent-player slot (Control-seeker archetype in the example party = Slot 4) is the off-screen driver of the reunion. If all five players are present, run Slot 4's convergence work in-fiction between sessions and open the episode with them delegating the on-site investigation to the others.

The party has been quietly rationalizing the strangeness for months in-game; the belief has cooled (cheapest-edit rationalization per world-truths). Sending them different pretext-invitations to Bodie is the arc's belief-reactivation beat.

Bodie SHP is a real California state park (Mono County) preserved in 'arrested decay.' Off-cell-signal, thirteen-mile washboard road, remote enough that the storm-trap is plausible. Alternate locations: Angel Island (shorter session, more accessible), Mount Shasta (more overtly genre).
inGameDate: A Saturday in late winter 2026-2027 (in-game); several months after the archivist's house.
